correctness.rationale: For orthonormal-row J and nonzero c, Gaussian invariance reduces to J=[I_r,0]. The independent Gaussian blocks of S produce x_coeff=(c,BG^†c), giving chi-square numerator d-r and Schur-complement denominator ell-r+1; a Gaussian nullspace representation produces x_geom=(c,-H2^†H1c) with numerator d-ell and the same denominator degrees. Both calculations follow from standard inverse-Wishart Schur complements. Gamma integration proves all finite-moment cases, nonintegrable boundaries and sharp tails. The ell=d zero-error exception, positivity and normalizations were separately checked. A local NumPy verifier reproduced 7214 finite algebraic/special-case identities from verify.py; no finite experiment serves as the proof of an infinite assertion.

Those works provide algorithmic or asymptotic frameworks, rather than this exact paired coefficient-metric versus physical-metric finite-sample law. Prior appearance in obscure specialized numerical inverse-problem literature remains possible.

value.rationale: Randomized subspace GN and rank-deficient linear model solvers need a concrete rule to choose one of many feasible updates. The coefficient minimum-norm rule depends on the random subspace basis, even when it spans the whole ambient space, unlike the physical norm rule. Exact error moments give a sharp oversampling threshold for a meaningful reliability metric, and quantify an otherwise hidden basis choice in a natural, reproducible finite model. The result is not merely a normalization check and does not claim a general nonlinear convergence theorem.
